exampleAnswers.title: Identifying the Period of a Function Given Its Graph

question.text: The graph of a periodic function $y = f(x)$ is shown above. What is the period of this function?
question.explanation:
Note that if we shift the graph $8$ units left or right, the graph remains unchanged.

On the other hand, if we shift the graph horizontally by any distance other than $8$ (or a multiple of $8$), we get a different graph.

Therefore, the period of the function is $8.$

question.text: Part of the graph of a function $y=f(x)$ with period $2$ is shown above. What is the graph of $y=f(x)$ on the interval $-4 \leq x \leq 4?$
question.explanation:
The graph above shows the function in the interval $0 \leq x \leq 2.$

Since this interval has length $2,$ and the period of the function is also $2,$ this interval represents a single period of the function.

Therefore, the function will consist of many copies of the shape shown above, shifted horizontally by multiples of $2.$

exampleAnswers.title: Inferring Values of a Periodic Function Given Its Graph

question.text: The graph of $y = f(x)$ is shown above. Given that $y = f(x)$ is periodic with period $3,$ what is the value of $f(30)?$
question.explanation:
Since the period is $3,$ if we add (or subtract) any multiple of $3$ from the input, the output stays the same.

So, we can keep subtracting $3$ from the input until we get to an input that we see in the graph:

\begin{align} f(30) &= f(30-3) \\[3pt] &= f(30-2\cdot3)\\[3pt] &= \cdots\\[3pt] &= f(30-10 \cdot 3) \\[3pt] &= f(0) \\[3pt] &= 1 \end{align}

question.text: The graph of $y = f(x)$ is shown above. Given that $y = f(x)$ is periodic with period $5,$ what is the value of $f(-37)?$
question.explanation:
Since the period is $5,$ if we add (or subtract) any multiple of $5$ from the input, the output stays the same.

So, we can keep adding $5$ to the input until we get to an input that we see in the graph:

\begin{align} f(-37) &= f(-37+5) \\[3pt] &= f(-37+2\cdot5)\\[3pt] &= \cdots\\[3pt] &= f(-37+8\cdot 5) \\[3pt] &= f(3) \\[3pt] &= 1 \end{align}

question.text: The graph of $y = f(x)$ is shown above. Given that $y = f(x)$ is periodic with period $5,$ what is the value of $f(132)?$
question.explanation:
Since the period is $5,$ if we add (or subtract) any multiple of $5$ from the input, the output stays the same.

So, we can keep subtracting $5$ from the input until we get to an input that we see in the graph:

\begin{align} f(132) &= f(132-5) \\[3pt] &= f(132-2\cdot 5)\\[3pt] &= \cdots\\[3pt] &= f(132- 26 \cdot 5) \\[3pt] &= f(2) \\[3pt] &= -2 \end{align}
